create.name: Charlotte Buddhist Vihara
create.bio:
Charlotte Buddhist Vihara is a small Theravada monastic residence and meditation house in north-east Charlotte, North Carolina, opened in 2013 and kept going by its lay community so that ordained Buddhist women can live and teach in the city. Its resident teacher, Ayya Sudhamma, grew up in Charlotte and practised law before going forth in 1998; she took novice vows with Bhante Gunaratana at the Bhavana Society, received full bhikkhuni ordination in Sri Lanka in 2003 and spent eight and a half years as resident monastic at a vihara in Greenville, South Carolina, before coming home. The vihara exists to house and support its monastics, who in turn offer the teaching freely.

Three times a week the nuns lead a talk and sitting session open to people of any religion or none, with no attempt to convert anyone; sessions are announced through the group's Meetup page. Alongside meditation instruction they teach Buddhist scripture, ethics and history, offer one-to-one spiritual guidance, and hold traditional South-east Asian observances such as full-moon days, Vesak and the Kathina robe offering. Everything is given without charge and the community lives on dana. Recorded talks and Pali chants are shared on the website and on its YouTube channel.

free_resources.title: Meditate with a Monk: weekly talks and meditation
free_resources.description: Three free sessions each week, on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and Saturday afternoon, each pairing a Dharma talk with sitting practice led by the resident nuns. Booking is through the vihara's Meetup group.

free_resources.title: Talks & Chants
free_resources.description: Audio recordings from the vihara: Pali chants honouring the early arahant nuns, with printed words, and recorded talks by Ayya Sudhamma on the Eightfold Path and the Sutta Nipata.
